deep.reconstruction:
This page is part of Euler's table in E283 giving the prime divisors of a²+1, here for a = 522 to 579. The table serves the search for very large primes of the form a²+1.

The convention is that only prime divisors smaller than a are listed. This is confirmed by checking entries:
- 526: 526²+1 = 276677 = 337·821. Only 337 is listed.
- 524: 274577 = 37·41·181, listed in full.

At most one prime factor of a²+1 can exceed a. So after removing the listed factors, the cofactor is meant to be either 1 or a single prime larger than a. A blank entry therefore declares a²+1 prime. The blanks here are 536, 544, 556, 570 and 576. They agree with the modern list of n with n²+1 prime (OEIS A005574).

The table is built by a sieve. If p | r²+1 with 0 < r < p, then p divides (kp ± r)²+1 for every k. Odd primes dividing a²+1 are ≡ 1 (mod 4). Prime powers are found the same way through square roots of −1 modulo p^k:
- 5³ appears at 557 and 568, since ±57 are the square roots of −1 mod 125.
- 13² appears at 577 (root 70 mod 169).
- 17² appears at 540 (root 251 mod 289).

I re-ran the sieve for every prime p ≡ 1 (mod 4) below 579, using its roots: 5:±2, 13:±5, 17:±4, 29:±12, 37:±6, 41:±9, 53:±23, 61:±11, 73:±27, 89:±34, 97:±22, 109:±33, 113:±15, 181:±19, 197:±14, 229:±107, 233:±89, 241:±64, 257:±16, 337:±148, 349:±136, 409:±143, 457:±109, and the rest. Every listed divisor checks out, for example 552²+1 = 5·149·409 and 565²+1 = 2·17·41·229. Every blank checks out too. The only failures are two missing divisors of 53, described under errors.
errors: a = 553: 553²+1 = 305810 = 2·5·53·577. Euler lists only '2. 5', omitting 53 (553 ≡ 23 mod 53). Under the table's convention this falsely implies that 30581 is prime.

The same slip occurs on the previous page at a = 507: 507²+1 = 2·5²·53·97, listed as '2. 5². 97'. So the residue class 30 mod 53 (507, 560) and 553 lost the factor 53 in this stretch. By contrast, 500 (53²·89), 606 and 613 do list 53.

ideas.what: Table of prime divisors of a²+1 (only those below a), used to identify primes of the form a²+1
ideas.modern_name: Sieve for primes of the form n²+1 (Landau's fourth problem); factor tables of n²+1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E283, 1762/64); later extended by Cunningham and others
ideas.where_published: E283, Novi Commentarii Acad. Sci. Petrop. 9 (1762/3, publ. 1764)

ideas.what: Periodicity: p | r²+1 implies p | (kp±r)²+1, including lifting to prime powers 5³, 13², 17²
ideas.modern_name: Quadratic sieve via square roots of −1 mod p^k (Hensel lifting)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine factor-table page. The only finding is two omitted factors of 53 (at 553 and 560), plus a related slip at 507 on the previous page. Such table errata may or may not have been recorded before; they have no conceptual significance.
transcription_corrections: Line 562 reads '5. 181. 349' (the dot between 181 and 349 is missing in the print). The factorization is correct: 5·181·349 = 315845.
Lines 557 and 568: the exponent on 5 is 3 (5³), consistent with the image and the arithmetic. The transcription is correct here.
